REGIS REPORT

15 September 2025

Cargo volumes at ICTSI’s (ICT PM) port in Mexico rebounded in Aug, recovering from the issues relating to the customs agency. Volumes reached 139k TEUs for the month, sharply up from the previous months and also up 12% YoY. 

 

+++

 

The country’s current account deficit reached US$5bn for 2Q25, equivalent to 4.0% of GDP. While this is narrower than the 5.2% of 2Q24, the 1H pace (3.9%) puts the FY25 CAD on track to exceed the 3.3% BSP forecast for 2025 and at risk of being higher than the 4.5% recorded in 2022, which was the widest in over 25 years.

 

+++

 

SM Investments (SM PM) is selling its interest in a holding firm (“Nagtahan Property Holdings”) which holds land in an area in the city of Manila to SM Prime (SMPH PM). We would be expecting SMPH to be developing the property into a condo complex.

 

+++

 

Among the those likely to be affected by the fallout from the corruption scandal engulfing the government today are the casinos. The Anti-Money Laundering Council, and possibly other agencies, is investigating the casino operators after reports that government employees linked to corruption issues gambled in a number of them. Tighter measures could eventually follow.

TRANSPORT
ICTSI’s Mexico port volumes rebound in August, as congestion eases
  • Data from Mexico’s port authority showed that container volumes at ICTSI’s port, Contecon Manzanillo (CMSA), rose 12% YoY to 139k TEUs in August, reversing declines in the past two months
    • We attribute the recovery to easing customs delays
  • Brings CMSA’s 8M25 volumes to 987k TEUs, up 4% YoY and trending below our full-year forecast of 1.63mn TEUs (+12% YoY)
    • To reach our forecast, volumes for the rest of the year will need to average 160k TEUs per month.
    • CMSA’s capacity today is at 1.7mn TEUs (~140k per month) and this will increase to “over 2mn TEUs” (~170k TEUs/month) by year-end (new berth will be completed by Sep 2025)
    • We estimate CMSA accounts for 12% of volumes, 20% of revenues and 24% of EBITDA
  • ICTSI trades at 10x/9x FY25E/FY26E EV/EBITDA, below peer median and historical average of 11x

 

 

 

MACRO
Current account deficit narrows to $5.0bn in 2Q25
  • The country's CA deficit narrowed to US$5.0bn (4.0% of GDP) in 2Q25 from the US$5.9bn (5.2% of GDP) deficit in 2Q24
  • The decline in the deficit was driven by the Philippines' narrower trade in goods gap
    • The trade-in-goods deficit was narrower by 5% YoY to US$16bn, given the faster growth in exports (+17%) vs. imports (+5%)
    • Net receipts from services trade fell 12% YoY to US$2.4bn, as imports grew 3% (to US$9.8bn) while exports fell 1% (to US$12.2bn)
      • The decline in services receipts was primarily due to higher travel imports given increased outbound travels as well as lower export receipts from a drop in tourist arrivals which was slightly offset by robust revenues from BPO activities

  • This brings the 1H25 CA deficit to 3.9% of GDP, wider than last year's 3.6%

  • For 2025, the BSP expects the country's CA deficit to hit US$16.3bn or 3.3% of GDP
    • Recall that in 2024, the country posted its second largest CA deficit at US$17.5bn (3.8% of GDP)—41.4% bigger than the 2023 deficit of US$12.4bn (2.8% of GDP)

 

 

 

PROPERTY
SM Investments to sell property to SM Prime
  • SM Investments disclosed that it will sell its entire equity interest in Nagtahan Property Holdings, a subsidiary with property in Nagtahan, Manila, to SM Prime
    • The size of the property and the selling price were not disclosed
    • We expect its value to be less than 1% of SM Prime’s NAV 
  • It also disclosed that it would form a subsidiary that will develop its Susana Heights property
    • It has about 260 hectares of land in Susana Heights
    • SM Prime previously said that it would develop the SM Group’s Susana Heights property
  • SMPH is trading at 44% discount to NAV, 1.5X FY25E P/B, and 15.1X FY25E P/E
GAMING
Anti-Money Laundering Council to investigate casinos
  • The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) said it would investigate casinos after former employees of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) reportedly gambled in various casino in PAGCOR Entertainment City
  • The casinos might have participated in money laundering
  • Furthermore, government officials are prohibited from entering the gaming areas of casinos
